This was originally done in the 30s down in the Delta - which is not actually where you might think. If you go to Natchez, Mississippi, you'll find that they're the Delta that they speak of. It's not the outflow into the ocean. It was sung by a fella named Howlin' Wolf and it wasn't recorded until sometime in the mid-50s (as far as I know) and was different than he probably first played it.

When he first played it, it was just a one chord song - you can do a lot with just one chord. This was seen in quite a bit of Delta Blues but the recorded version was done after his move to Chicago and so you ended up with the song being a Chicago Blues song.

Why did I choose this version? Few folks have ever heard it and it's really lovely. Lots and lots of people have since recorded it but this one is seldom heard. It's on the Best of Bear's Choice Vol I (there was no II) and that's probably one of my favorite Grateful Dead albums. So, I figured I'd share this one.

Anyhow, if you go to Natchez, you can go to the Blues Museum and that's a pretty nifty place. They're just a small place but they have some nice exhibits and it's free to enter (though they do ask for a donation). You can hear some pretty rare stuff there. Well, probably not really rare in the day of digital file transmission, but seldom heard. While you're there, eat. The food is delicious.
